claims.statement: Allocation rule set v18 went live at 22:00 and orders became stuck at 06:00 on the east node only, establishing a temporal and operational correlation
claims.limitation: Correlation does not confirm causation; v18 passed regression tests

claims.statement: Every stuck order is flagged as a 'split-reservation exception' by the overnight allocator
claims.limitation: The meaning and downstream handling of this flag is not yet known

claims.statement: Inventory Control confirms that allocation totals reconcile and nothing looks wrong on their side
claims.limitation: Reconciliation at the totals level does not rule out per-order inventory state issues

claims.statement: Orders are stuck in a handoff between allocation (east node, marked awaiting pickup) and carrier pickup collection; root cause could lie in either allocation logic, carrier feed delivery, or observability blind spots
claims.limitation: Multiple competing mechanisms remain plausible; insufficient data to discriminate

next_action.rationale: Every stuck order shares the 'split-reservation exception' flag. Understanding what this flag means, how it is generated by v18, and how orders bearing it are handed off to the carrier scheduling system will either confirm a v18 defect or redirect focus to carrier integration or observability gaps. This is the highest-leverage diagnostic given the universal presence of the flag.
